claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if later TPU generations abandon OCS-based interconnect or if disclosed cost share rises materially (indicating the layer stopped being cheap leverage).
claims.statement: Per Google's own TPU v4 paper, OCSes and underlying optical components are <5% of system cost and <3% of system power, while enabling 4x larger supercomputer scale, topology reconfiguration and availability gains — an asymmetric cost-to-leverage bottleneck layer in TPU interconnect.

source_doc.permission_basis: Public arXiv preprint; URL and short excerpts only.
source_doc.title: TPU v4: An Optically Reconfigurable Supercomputer for Machine Learning (Jouppi et al., ISCA 2023)

sources.quote: OCSes and underlying optical components are <5% of system cost and <3% of system power.

The resulting Google Palomar OCS is based on 3D Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) mirrors that switch in milliseconds. They employ circulators to send light both ways in a fiber, halving the number of required ports and cables.
The Palomar OCS is 136x136 (128 ports plus 8 spares for link testing and repairs)
